prompted_for: Home section 'Start from where your project is': project situations (no URS, budget, draft URS, qualifying suppliers, qualification, upgrade, production stopped); first prompt (blueprint style): manifold hub with situations as pipes radiating from one junction to equipment destinations
composition: wide panel on deep navy inside a sheet border with edge ticks
framed headline box top centre with a thin drop line to the hub
one isometric junction box at the centre
seven pipes radiate from the hub on isometric diagonals to equipment vignettes around the edges
situation labels set along each pipe, rotated to the pipe angle
layout_devices: radiating pipe routes as menu items
labels running along pipes at isometric angles
boxed headline with leader to hub
palette: pale blue-white line art and text
typography: light-to-regular sans headline in an outlined box
regular sans labels rotated along pipe angles
line_and_texture: double-line pipes with fittings and valves
motifs: elevated water tank on a stand (feed)
motion_implied: selecting a situation lights its pipe from hub to destination
water flows out of the hub along the chosen branch
t2i_keywords: drawing sheet border with tick marks
t2i_prompt: A wide web page section drawn as an engineering blueprint on a deep navy background with a thin sheet border, edge ticks and a title block bottom right. At the centre an isometric manifold junction box; several double-line pipes in pale blue-white hairlines radiate from it on isometric diagonals, each ending at a small isometric equipment vignette near the edges. Each pipe carries a short label set along its angle: <CONTENT>. Small steel-blue arrows show flow outward. A boxed light sans-serif headline sits top centre with a thin leader to the hub. Flat, no shading, no people.
signature_idea: A situation router drawn as a manifold: every starting point is a pipe branching from one hub, so choosing your situation means choosing a route.
strengths: original, memorable routing metaphor that matches a water company
maps cleanly to an interactive router (hover lights a branch)
consistent blueprint language with the other home sections
weaknesses: rotated labels along diagonals are hard to read and inaccessible as text
equipment at the pipe ends is arbitrary and does not explain the situation
crowded edges, little calm negative space
no limestone surface; heavy if repeated across a page
brand_fit_why: Navy, hairlines and steel-blue arrows fit, but rotated labels, density and decorative equipment undercut 'precise, calm, space as a material'.
